blocks.text: Mary Hill Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Mary Hill is the south-side hillside above the Fraser River lowland, around Mary Hill Road, Western, Eastern and Lamprey Drives; no City sub-area boundary is published.
Wilson Avenue is the north edge, with Port Coquitlam Station there; the Mary Hill Bypass (Highway 7B) runs along the south/west edges.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: City-wide, in full here only: Zoning Bylaw, 2008, No. 3630 governs house lots, in Residential Small-Scale zones RS1–RS4.

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH): three to six units without rezoning on RS1–RS4 lots; number set by lot size, location and transit. A duplex, larger project or accessory dwelling unit needs an SSMUH Development Permit first.
No separate Mary Hill plan: Official Community Plan Bylaw, 2013, No. 3838 (2013).

blocks.text: Mary Hill Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Routley Park, 1570 Western Drive, has the Routley wading pool; Robert Hope Park, 2137 Lamprey Drive, has the Robert Hope pool.
Heritage Resource Inventory: 1900–2100 Fraser Avenue are early Flint-neighbourhood houses — check heritage status first.
Suites are billed as an additional unit; 2026 exemption deduction $964, or $482 at the parent rate, by December 31.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Houses: development and new projects

items.t: City-wide, in full here only: Housing Accelerator Fund — federal award up to $10.3 million (2025) plus $1.7 million (March 2026); 1,183 units aimed for in three years. STATUS: Year 1 report January 8, 2026; read 2026-11-03.

City-wide, in full here only: Gates Park soccer hub, 2300 Reeve Street — more than half complete; completion anticipated before June 2026, Phase 2 by September 2026. STATUS: December 17, 2025; check current.
Streetlights, Eastern Drive at Western and Pooley: STATUS design May 2026; read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: City-wide, in full here only: 2026 residential tax, Bylaw No. 4441, $2.1985 per $1,000 general plus $0.0552 Metro Vancouver line; due July 2, 2026.
City-wide utilities, 2026: single unit $646 water / $648 sewer; additional unit $481 / $483; due March 31, 2026, penalties after March 31 and June 1; solid waste on the tax notice.
Port Coquitlam is a provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax taxable area; owners must declare annually even if exempt.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Houses: getting around

items.t: Route 170 loop: Station via Wilson, Shaughnessy, Pitt River Road, Eastern/Western Drives, back via Mary Hill Road.
Port Coquitlam Station, 2125 Kingsway Avenue, north edge: West Coast Express park-and-ride, 267 spaces, $3 daily / $60 monthly.

blocks.text: Mary Hill Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check flood status per lot: two City floodplains, Fraser/Pitt and Coquitlam River; dikes and pump stations are patrolled.
Much of the city sits behind dikes raised in 2007; low bypass lots need the same check.

blocks.text: Mary Hill home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

26 houses sold in Mary Hill with a median price of $1,305,000 (the middle half sold between $1,231,250 and $1,363,250), taking a median of 18 days to sell at 96.7% of the last list price; 15% sold above list. They had a median $537 per square foot, a median year built of 1971 and a median lot of 7,444 square feet.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Mary Hill

Mostly detached homes on the hill south of downtown, with the Fraser River below, make Mary Hill Port Coquitlam’s established south side. École Mary Hill Elementary offers Early French Immersion, a big draw for families, and ƛ̓éxətəm Regional Park (formerly Colony Farm) and the river trails are close by. It suits families and value-minded buyers looking at older homes on bigger lots.
